web_title: 6. Multi-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: Financial Forensics — Margin Trajectory, Goodwill Weight & TEU Dilution
question: How have BrightSpring's P&L, cash conversion, ROIC, debt profile, and diluted share count evolved from FY2023 through Q3 2026, and where do the accounting and capital-structure risks sit?

epigraph.quote: Our third quarter results again reflect the commitment of our team to patient care and operational execution across our Pharmacy and Provider businesses.
epigraph.author: Jon Rousseau, CEO, BrightSpring Health Services (Q3 2026 Earnings Release)

web_blocks.html: Reading BrightSpring's financial history requires focusing on continuing operations, which exclude the sold Community Living unit [1, 26]. From FY2023 to FY2025, continuing revenue compounded at a ~29.6% two-year CAGR [1, 3]. Sales grew from ~$7,691 million in FY2023 to $10,072.2 million in FY2024 (+31.0%) and $12,910.6 million in FY2025 (+28.2%) [1, 3]. Momentum held firm across the first nine months of 2026: Q3 2026 revenue reached $4,213.2 million (+26.4% YoY), bringing 9M 2026 continuing revenue to $11,700.1 million (+25.0% YoY vs. $9,359.9 million) [26, 27]. Management guides full-year 2026 revenue to $15.9–$16.125 billion [27].

Profitability inflected sharply in FY2025 and 2026 as scale absorbed fixed overhead and debt paydown cut interest drag [1, 26]. FY2024 posted a $(68.9) million GAAP net loss [1]. In FY2025, GAAP operating income more than doubled from $112.3 million to $295.3 million, and GAAP net income swung to +$104.8 million [1]. Across 9M 2026, GAAP operating income more than doubled to $412.3 million (+120.3% YoY vs. $187.1 million), and continuing net income reached $261.7 million ($100.8 million in Q3 2026 alone) [26, 27]. However, earnings-quality forensics show that 9M 2026 GAAP continuing net income benefited from an unusually low 14.4% effective tax rate (versus 25.4% before discrete items, per Note 8) because $33.0 million of discrete excess tax benefits from stock-based compensation vesting and exercises flowed through the tax line [26].

web_blocks.title: 6.2 Balance Sheet, Goodwill Weight, ROIC vs. WACC & TEU Dilution

web_blocks.html: BrightSpring's balance sheet shows both its roll-up history and subtle footnote complexities [1, 26]. At September 30, 2026, total assets stood at $6,266.6 million, carrying $2,537.1 million of goodwill and $491.7 million of net intangibles ($3,028.8 million combined, or 48% of assets and 139% of $2,176.6 million total equity) [26]. Amedisys/LHC provisional purchase accounting allocated 92% of the $238.5 million price to goodwill ($165.4 million) and intangibles ($62.9 million), with three branches still pending closing [26]. That heavy goodwill denominator explains why headline ROIC sits at 7.58%, alongside 15.57% ROE and 5.05% ROA [18, 26]. Note 9 also reveals rising operating reserve balances YTD. General and professional liability reserves rose 48.8% to $48.7 million, partially offset by $31.5 million of insurance recoveries [26]. Health insurance reserves jumped 84.6% to $28.4 million [26]. Accrued legal settlements and fees more than doubled to $22.8 million, while checks in excess of cash stood at $21.4 million [26].

On the liability side, the $810.9 million Community Living proceeds funded a $300.0 million paydown and May 28, 2026 Tranche B-6 repricing (SOFR + 2.00%, due February 21, 2031) [4, 5, 26]. Carrying debt stood at $2,182.1 million ($2,237.6 million gross principal less $55.6 million issuance costs) against $717.8 million in cash [26]. That cut net leverage to 1.79x [26, 27]. Crucially, Q3 10-Q Note 6 and Item 3 show only $1,000 million of interest rate swaps (3.18%–3.33% fixed through September 2028), leaving ~$1.21 billion floating-rate—each +100 bps in SOFR cuts annual net income and cash flow by $12.1 million [26]. On the equity side, 3,313,010 TEU shares already early-converted in 9M 2026 (plus 2,831,467 in 9M 2025) [26]. Per Notes 7 and 10, the 26.2 million minimum TEU shares are already baked into basic EPS (207.0 million Q3 basic shares) [6, 26]. The extra 4.6 million variable band (up to 30.8 million) only triggers between $13.00 and $15.28 [6, 26]. Meanwhile, KKR still holds 26,829,880 shares (13.6%) [29].

web_blocks.title: 6.3 Earnings Quality, Non-Cash Amortization & Working-Capital Cadence

web_blocks.html: Cash-flow forensics confirm real cash generation alongside two critical working-capital and tax nuances [1, 26]. In FY2025, CFO ($490.2 million) beat GAAP net income ($104.8 million) by $385.4 million [1]. In 9M 2026, reported CFO was $371.2 million ($204.3 million in Q3 alone), despite absorbing $97.0 million of cash taxes and $17.0 million of transaction costs from the Community Living sale [26]. Without that $114.0 million divestiture drag, underlying 9M CFO was ~$485 million—yet $143.4 million of that cash flow came from shrinking on-balance-sheet inventories ($815.2 million to $671.6 million) via a new $111.6 million off-balance-sheet supplier consignment arrangement [26].

Balance-sheet discipline therefore hinges on four gauges [1, 6, 26]. First, net accounts receivable ($1,216.4 million, ~26 days DSO) and trade accounts payable ($1,232.3 million) must stay synchronized alongside the $111.6 million consignment inventory so wholesaler terms never tighten unexpectedly [26]. Second, investors should normalize GAAP net income for the 14.4% 9M effective tax rate (25.4% ex-discrete SBC benefits) and monitor $91.8 million of 9M Adjusted EBITDA add-backs ($50.5 million SBC, $15.6 million integration, $25.8 million restructuring) [26]. Third, $1.21 billion of unhedged Term Loan B-6 debt preserves sensitivity to SOFR [26]. Fourth, KKR's 26.83 million remaining shares (13.6%) and February 1, 2027 final TEU settlement mark the remaining structural cap-table milestones [6, 29].

book_paragraphs: Let's put BrightSpring's financial statements under a forensic microscope. Four realities in Chapter 6 separate a surface bull case from serious underwriting. First, look at the cash-flow rebound: in FY2024, Operating Cash Flow was just $23.8 million because the ~$120 million Silver settlement and working-capital timing ate nearly all operating cash. Skeptics claimed the model could not convert earnings into cash. Then in FY2025, Operating Cash Flow surged to $490.2 million against $104.8 million of GAAP net income, yielding $394.7 million of Free Cash Flow after $95.5 million of CapEx. In 2026, 9M CFO hit $371.2 million, with $204.3 million generated in Q3 alone.

Second, trace the GAAP profit inflection—and its tax-rate nuance—from FY2024 through Q3 2026. In FY2024, BrightSpring posted a $(68.9) million GAAP net loss from continuing operations. In FY2025, operating income more than doubled to $295.3 million (2.3% margin), net interest fell 17.4% to $157.3 million, and GAAP net income swung to +$104.8 million. Through the first nine months of 2026, continuing revenue rose 25.0% to $11,700.1 million, operating income jumped 120.3% to $412.3 million (3.5% margin), and continuing net income reached $261.7 million ($100.8 million in Q3 alone). Yet Note 8 of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q flags an important quality-of-earnings footnote: 9M 2026's GAAP effective tax rate dropped to 14.4% (against a 25.4% annual rate before discrete items) solely because $33.0 million of excess tax benefits from employee stock-option exercises and RSU vestings boosted the tax line.

Third, inspect the asset side of the balance sheet before trusting headline return ratios. At year-end 2025, out of $6,413.3 million in total assets, BrightSpring held $2,545.7 million of goodwill and $557.6 million of net intangibles. That $3,103.3 million of acquisition paper equaled 48% of assets and 166% of stockholders' equity ($1,875.1 million). Because that large denominator sits on the books, consolidated ROIC is a modest 7.58% (with 15.57% ROE and 5.05% ROA), near a 7%–8% healthcare cost of capital. Organic returns on Onco360 LDD launches are much higher, yet historical goodwill reminds us why management must stay disciplined on deal prices—as it did when buying 107 DOJ-forced Amedisys branches for $239 million.

Fourth, check the debt stack, swap coverage, and upcoming share-count events. After the $810.9 million Community Living proceeds and May 28, 2026's $300.0 million paydown and Tranche B-6 repricing (SOFR + 2.00%, due February 21, 2031), total carrying debt at September 30, 2026 stood at $2,182.1 million ($2,237.6 million gross principal) against $717.8 million of cash, cutting net leverage to 1.79x. Note 6 and Item 3 disclose that BrightSpring carries $1,000 million of fixed-rate swaps (3.18%–3.33% through September 2028), leaving ~$1.21 billion unhedged floating debt where a 1% SOFR increase reduces annual net income and cash flow by $12.1 million. On the share count, 3,313,010 TEU shares already converted early during 9M 2026 (plus 2,831,467 in 9M 2025). The 26.2 million minimum TEU shares are already included in basic EPS (207.0 million Q3 shares), and the extra 4.6 million variable band only applies if the average stock value sits between $13.00 and $15.28 at the February 1, 2027 settlement—while KKR still holds 26,829,880 shares (13.6%).

Tie the P&L trajectory back to the cash-flow bridge to see the operating leverage clearly. From FY2023 to FY2025, continuing revenue compounded nearly 30% annually—from ~$7,691 million to $10,072.2 million and $12,910.6 million. Nine-month 2026 revenue (~$11,683 million across $3.6B, $3.87B, and $4.213B quarters) puts full-year 2026 guidance at $15.9 to $16.125 billion. Over that same period, Adjusted EBITDA is scaling from $460.2 million in FY2024 to $617.6 million in FY2025 and $850–$860 million guided for FY2026. Rapid scale, mix-driven gross-profit gains ($162.9 million non-cash D&A and <1% CapEx), and falling interest form the financial engine we value in Part II. Note also that FY2023 Adjusted EBITDA of $537.8 million included a ~$30 million one-time Quality Incentive Payment, or $508 million excluding it. Against that clean $508 million baseline, FY2026 guidance represents nearly 68% cumulative EBITDA growth in three years.

Notice two subtle working-capital and cash-flow details in 9M 2026. Reported 9M operating cash flow was $371.2 million ($204.3 million in Q3 alone), even after paying $97.0 million of cash taxes and $17.0 million of transaction costs for the Community Living divestiture. Stripping out that $114.0 million divestiture outflow puts underlying 9M CFO near $485 million—yet $143.4 million of that cash came from shrinking on-balance-sheet inventories ($815.2 million to $671.6 million) via a new $111.6 million off-balance-sheet supplier consignment program. Also keep an eye on Note 9 accrued reserves: general and professional liability reserves climbed 48.8% YTD to $48.7 million, health insurance reserves jumped 84.6% to $28.4 million, legal settlements accrued doubled to $22.8 million, and checks in excess of cash stood at $21.4 million.

Let's also check working-capital intensity from another angle: days sales outstanding (DSO) and inventory turns. Because BrightSpring bills commercial insurers, PBMs, Medicare Part D plans, and state Medicaid agencies across $16 billion of annualized revenue, even a two-day slip in DSO ties up roughly $88 million of cash. At September 30, 2026, net accounts receivable stood at $1,216.4 million—roughly 26 days of Q3 annualized sales. That is remarkably tight for a specialty and home-health operator, especially compared with hospital or skilled-nursing peers that routinely wait 45 to 60 days for reimbursement. Keeping DSOs under 30 days while growing specialty revenue above 30% is one of the quietest operational achievements in BrightSpring's turnaround.

Equally important is capital expenditure discipline. In FY2025, BrightSpring spent just $95.5 million on CapEx against $12,910.6 million of continuing revenue—less than 0.75% of sales. Why is CapEx so low? Because specialty oncology pharmacies and home-health branches do not require billion-dollar factories or hospital real estate. Growth CapEx goes primarily into pharmacy automation, cold-chain packaging, cleanroom compounding hubs for infusion, and clinical workflow software. That asset-light physical footprint explains why $490.2 million of FY2025 operating cash flow converted into $394.7 million of free cash flow, and why incremental organic revenue requires very little fixed-asset reinvestment.

Think about what that combination—sub-1% CapEx intensity plus falling interest expense—does to BrightSpring's free cash flow trajectory over the next three years. In FY2024, heavy debt service and the $120 million PharMerica Silver settlement consumed nearly all operating cash flow. By FY2026, with net debt down to ~$1.46 billion and leverage at 1.79x, BrightSpring's debt-service burden has shrunk dramatically. Every $100 million of incremental Adjusted EBITDA now drops roughly $55 million to $60 million straight into free cash flow, assuming working capital stays disciplined and tax rates normalize around 22% to 24%.

Before we leave the financial statements, let's do one final sanity check on earnings quality: stock-based compensation and non-GAAP adjustments. Like most recent private-equity-backed IPOs, BrightSpring adds back share-based compensation, transaction/integration costs, and debt extinguishment losses to reach Adjusted EBITDA. Our rule is simple: never value a company on Adjusted EBITDA without checking how closely operating cash flow tracks it. Across FY2025, operating cash flow ($490.2 million) equaled 79% of Adjusted EBITDA ($617.6 million), and free cash flow ($394.7 million) equaled 64%—strong cash confirmation that the underlying business economics are real, not accounting noise.

One final balance-sheet nuance deserves your attention before we turn to valuation: lease liabilities and contingent acquisition obligations. Operating across 30 states of home health branches and specialty fulfillment hubs means BrightSpring carries real-estate and fleet lease commitments alongside earnout liabilities from tuck-in branch purchases. Yet because those branches generate high cash-on-cash payback with minimal maintenance CapEx, lease obligations scale proportionally with revenue rather than creating hidden off-balance-sheet distress. Combined with $717.8 million of cash on hand, $2,182.1 million of total debt, and no near-term maturity wall after the Q2 2026 First Lien modification, BrightSpring enters FY2027 with the cleanest balance sheet in its public history, giving management ample flexibility to fund organic LDD launches without issuing equity, without straining liquidity, and while keeping dry powder for opportunistic branch tuck-ins.

With Chapter 6 complete, you have the full price-blind business, competitive, and financial foundation. You know how BrightSpring evolved from a leveraged ResCare and PharMerica roll-up into a 155-LDD specialty pharmacy and 30-state home health platform. You see why a 2.3%–3.5% GAAP operating margin converts into substantial Free Cash Flow, how 68.2% government payor concentration, $111.6 million of consignment inventory, and CMS's November 2026 rules shape unit risk, and how $3.03 billion of goodwill and intangibles tempers ROIC to 7.58% while leverage falls to 1.79x. You also have the exact balance-sheet watchpoints: $1.21 billion of unhedged SOFR debt, normalizing the 14.4% tax rate toward 25.4%, KKR's remaining 26.83 million shares (13.6%), and February 1, 2027's final TEU settlement. Next, Part II brings valuation, market expectations, and risk-reward into focus.

book_callouts.title: Goodwill Denominator vs. Incremental Economics
book_callouts.text: A 7.58% headline ROIC on $3.10B of goodwill and intangibles does not mean the underlying specialty pharmacy or home health branches earn 7.6% incremental returns—it reflects the historical LBO purchase price. Still, it reminds you that disciplined M&A pricing is essential so future roll-ups don't dilute economic returns.
